options.content:
**What each real Trainium scenario shows.** Use **Demo dashboards** to focus on one task, or use the links `scripts/demo.sh` prints. Pick a run in **Run**; navigation carries the filters and time range.

| Scenario | Incident log | Panels |
|---|---|---|
| `healthy` | none | *Training loss* falls; *Held-out exact match, generated* climbs to about 70-75% (teacher-forced: about 85%) |
| `bad_lr` | DIVERGENCE, ROLLBACK to checkpoint 50 | *Learning rate* x1000 at step 70; loss and gradient norm hit 1e6 (NaN), then recover as attempt 2 |
| `healthy_grpo` | none, or HELDOUT_DECLINE, ADVISE if held-out accuracy declines (overfitting); response `noted: ...; kept GRPO step N ...` | *GRPO training reward* ~0.95; *Sampled SQL* all **correct**; *grader gap* 0 throughout; the run keeps going |
| `reward_hacking` | REWARD_HACKING, STOP | Held-out accuracy falls while reward holds or climbs; the *grader gap* rises from below 0; paid-but-wrong rises, filters fall; *Sampled SQL* reward-1 rows marked **wrong**; the run stops |
| `reward_hacking_unwatched` | REWARD_HACKING, response `ignored (watchdog off)` | Same, but the run keeps going |

**InfluxDB is the control plane:** each incident row is a command (ROLLBACK, STOP, or ADVISE, which never stops a run); trainers poll `incident` for their run (query node) and write back `control_ack`. **response** in the *Incident log* is the trainer's answer.
**Cluster:** InfluxDB 3 Enterprise; writes on the ingest node, reads (polls, this dashboard) on the query node, compaction on its own node. The **Data plane** row at the bottom shows both sides.
Empty panels that need a specific run say which.

panels.title: Open incidents
panels.description: Incidents with an OPEN transition and no RESOLVED transition in the time range. RESOLVED means the detector went quiet; check the trainer's response to see whether a command was applied.

panels.title: Incident log: Flink decides, InfluxDB carries the command, the trainer responds
panels.description: Each OPEN row is a command: the trainer reads it from this table (reader endpoint) and responds. ROLLBACK and STOP change the run; ADVISE (HELDOUT_DECLINE: held-out accuracy fell but the grader agreed with the strict check, likely overfitting) lets the run continue, and the trainer keeps its best evaluation's adapters. response is what the trainer reported doing (control_ack), joined on incident_id; seen after is the time from the event that triggered the detection to the trainer reading the row from InfluxDB.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT i.time, i.state, i.type, i.run_id, i.action, i.arg, a.outcome AS response,
       round(a.seen_latency_ms) AS "seen after", i.onset_step, i.step, i.severity, i.message
FROM (SELECT time, state, type, run_id, incident_id, action, action_arg AS arg, onset_step, step, severity, message
      FROM incident WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 100) i
LEFT JOIN (SELECT incident_id, outcome, seen_latency_ms FROM control_ack WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}') a
  ON a.incident_id = i.incident_id
ORDER BY i.time DESC

panels.title: Control loop through InfluxDB: from the triggering event to the trainer's response
panels.description: One pair of dots per command. Seen by the trainer: telemetry -> Kinesis -> Flink detects -> incident written to InfluxDB (ingest node) -> visible on the query node -> the trainer's next poll. Trainer responded: the trainer handles commands between steps, so this adds the rest of the current step (a GRPO step takes 6-8 s). A response can report an applied or ignored command; read the Incident log for the outcome.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time, 'seen by the trainer' AS series, seen_latency_ms AS value FROM control_ack
WHERE seen_latency_ms IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}'
UNION ALL
SELECT time, 'trainer responded' AS series, apply_latency_ms AS value FROM control_ack
WHERE apply_latency_ms IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}'
ORDER BY time

defaults.noValue: No commands in the time range

panels.title: Numerical failure: is the model failing to learn?
Training loss (mean across ranks)
panels.description: Log scale. Non-finite losses (NaN) are plotted at 1e6.

targets.rawSql: SELECT time, scenario, loss FROM step_summary WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' ORDER BY time
SELECT time, scenario, grad_norm FROM step_summary WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' ORDER BY time

panels.title: Layer gradient norms (bad learning-rate runs)
panels.description: One line per layer (12 simulated, 28 in the real Qwen2.5-1.5B): the norm across its LoRA modules, rank 0. In a divergence, see which layers blow up first.

targets.rawSql: SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '1 second', time) AS time, layer, sqrt(sum(grad_norm * grad_norm)) AS grad_norm FROM layer_stats WHERE scenario LIKE '%bad_lr' AND (rank IS NULL OR rank = '0') AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' GROUP BY 1, layer ORDER BY 1
SELECT time, scenario, lr FROM train_step WHERE rank = '0' AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' ORDER BY time

panels.title: Held-out eval loss (Trainium SFT)
panels.description: Real Trainium SFT runs. Teacher-forced on held-out questions whose query shapes, some phrasings, and literals never appear in training; no SQL is executed.

targets.rawSql: SELECT time, scenario, eval_loss FROM eval WHERE eval_loss IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' ORDER BY time

panels.title: Held-out exact match, generated (Trainium SFT)
panels.description: Real Trainium SFT runs. The model writes the whole SQL itself (greedy decoding) for 32 held-out questions with unseen query shapes, phrasings, and literals; counts exact matches with the gold SQL after whitespace normalization. Stricter than teacher-forced exact match, where the model is shown the correct SQL so far at every token.

targets.rawSql: SELECT time, scenario, gen_exact_match FROM eval WHERE gen_exact_match IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' ORDER BY time

panels.title: Held-out exact match, teacher-forced (Trainium SFT)
panels.description: Real Trainium SFT runs. Teacher-forced on held-out questions whose query shapes, some phrasings, and literals never appear in training; no SQL is executed.

targets.rawSql: SELECT time, scenario, exact_match FROM eval WHERE exact_match IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' ORDER BY time

panels.title: Objective failure (GRPO runs): is the model learning the wrong thing?
Reward vs held-out accuracy: what the grader pays against what is right
panels.description: Dashed: GRPO training reward (10-step moving average). Solid with points: held-out SQL execution accuracy (64 questions the model never trains on). Reward hacking is the gap opening between them. Pick a run in Run to isolate it.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time, concat(scenario, ' reward') AS series,
       AVG(reward) OVER (PARTITION BY run_id ORDER BY time ROWS BETWEEN 9 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS value
FROM rl_step WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}'
UNION ALL
SELECT time, concat(scenario, ' held-out accuracy') AS series, exec_accuracy AS value
FROM eval WHERE exec_accuracy IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}'
ORDER BY time

defaults.noValue: GRPO runs only: run healthy_grpo, reward_hacking, or reward_hacking_unwatched

panels.title: GRPO run outcomes: training progress and STOP response
panels.description: One row per run: how far GRPO progressed, best and latest held-out accuracy in the selected time range, and the trainer's latest STOP and ADVISE responses. Both hacking runs receive STOP; only the watched trainer obeys it. A run whose held-out accuracy declines while its grader agrees with the strict check (healthy_grpo overfitting) receives ADVISE instead: the trainer keeps its best evaluation's adapters and keeps training. Best observed accuracy is the highest evaluation in the selected window.

targets.rawSql:
WITH progress AS (
  SELECT run_id, scenario, max(step) AS last_grpo_step
  FROM rl_step WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' GROUP BY run_id, scenario
), best_eval AS (
  SELECT run_id, max(exec_accuracy) AS best_accuracy
  FROM eval WHERE exec_accuracy IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' GROUP BY run_id
), latest_eval AS (
  SELECT run_id, exec_accuracy,
         row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY run_id ORDER BY time DESC) AS evaluation_order
  FROM eval WHERE exec_accuracy IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}'
), stop_response AS (
  SELECT run_id, outcome,
         row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY run_id ORDER BY time DESC) AS response_order
  FROM control_ack WHERE action = 'STOP' AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}'
), advise_response AS (
  SELECT run_id, outcome,
         row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY run_id ORDER BY time DESC) AS response_order
  FROM control_ack WHERE action = 'ADVISE' AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}'
), commands AS (
  SELECT run_id, max(CASE WHEN action = 'STOP' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS got_stop,
         max(CASE WHEN action = 'ADVISE' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS got_advise
  FROM incident WHERE state = 'OPEN' AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' GROUP BY run_id
)
SELECT p.scenario, p.run_id, p.last_grpo_step AS "Last GRPO step",
       b.best_accuracy AS "Best observed accuracy", e.exec_accuracy AS "Latest accuracy",
       COALESCE(a.outcome, CASE WHEN c.got_stop = 1 THEN 'not acknowledged: the run had ended' END) AS "STOP response",
       COALESCE(v.outcome, CASE WHEN c.got_advise = 1 THEN 'not acknowledged: the run had ended' END) AS "ADVISE response"
FROM progress p
LEFT JOIN best_eval b ON b.run_id = p.run_id
LEFT JOIN latest_eval e ON e.run_id = p.run_id AND e.evaluation_order = 1
LEFT JOIN stop_response a ON a.run_id = p.run_id AND a.response_order = 1
LEFT JOIN advise_response v ON v.run_id = p.run_id AND v.response_order = 1
LEFT JOIN commands c ON c.run_id = p.run_id
ORDER BY p.run_id DESC

panels.title: How the model games the grader (GRPO runs)
Grader disagreement: paid but wrong vs correct but unpaid, and the grader gap
panels.description: Per GRPO step, share of sampled candidates (10-step moving average). Correct but unpaid (dashed): a right answer the lenient grader paid 0, usually a correct query that returns no rows. That is the pressure. Paid but wrong (solid): the lenient grader paid a wrong answer. That is the exploit. Both are measured against the lenient grader, even in healthy_grpo, whose training grader is the strict one. Grader gap (dotted, right axis): the training reward minus exec_match, the share of the same candidates that are strictly correct (10-step moving average); for the lenient grader it is paid but wrong minus correct but unpaid. It is what the watchdog checks when held-out accuracy falls: 0 for an honest grader (a decline is likely overfitting: HELDOUT_DECLINE, ADVISE), rising for one being gamed (REWARD_HACKING, STOP). Simulated runs report only the gap.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time, concat(scenario, ' paid but wrong') AS series,
       AVG(paid_but_wrong_rate) OVER (PARTITION BY run_id ORDER BY time ROWS BETWEEN 9 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS value
FROM rl_step WHERE paid_but_wrong_rate IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}'
UNION ALL
SELECT time, concat(scenario, ' correct but unpaid') AS series,
       AVG(honest_unpaid_rate) OVER (PARTITION BY run_id ORDER BY time ROWS BETWEEN 9 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS value
FROM rl_step WHERE honest_unpaid_rate IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}'
UNION ALL
SELECT time, concat(scenario, ' grader gap') AS series,
       AVG(reward - exec_match) OVER (PARTITION BY run_id ORDER BY time ROWS BETWEEN 9 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS value
FROM rl_step WHERE reward IS NOT NULL AND exec_match IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}'
ORDER BY time

defaults.noValue: GRPO runs only: run healthy_grpo, reward_hacking, or reward_hacking_unwatched

panels.title: Held-out accuracy by question type
panels.description: Held-out execution accuracy at each evaluation, by question type. No data (dashed): the correct answer is empty. The loophole is exactly these: a model that learns to always return rows gets them wrong first. Has data (solid): every other question. Time window (dotted): questions over a relative time range, such as "last 15 minutes", whose answer depends on keeping the time filter; each also counts as no data or has data.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time, concat(scenario, ' has data') AS series, exec_accuracy_has_data AS value
FROM eval WHERE exec_accuracy_has_data IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}'
UNION ALL
SELECT time, concat(scenario, ' no data') AS series, exec_accuracy_no_data AS value
FROM eval WHERE exec_accuracy_no_data IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}'
UNION ALL
SELECT time, concat(scenario, ' time window') AS series, exec_accuracy_window AS value
FROM eval WHERE exec_accuracy_window IS NOT NULL AND coalesce(window_questions, 1) > 0 AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}'
ORDER BY time

defaults.noValue: GRPO runs only: run healthy_grpo, reward_hacking, or reward_hacking_unwatched

panels.title: Filters per generated query
panels.description: Average WHERE conditions in the sampled SQL (10-step moving average). Falling means the model is dropping filters to make queries return rows.

targets.rawSql: SELECT time, scenario, AVG(filters_mean) OVER (PARTITION BY scenario, run_id ORDER BY time ROWS BETWEEN 9 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS filters_mean FROM rl_step WHERE filters_mean IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' ORDER BY time

defaults.noValue: GRPO runs only: run healthy_grpo, reward_hacking, or reward_hacking_unwatched

panels.title: Queries that filter on a host or sensor
panels.description: Share of sampled queries with a host = or sensor = condition (10-step moving average). Hosts and sensors are where most no-data answers come from.

targets.rawSql: SELECT time, scenario, AVG(entity_filter_rate) OVER (PARTITION BY scenario, run_id ORDER BY time ROWS BETWEEN 9 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS entity_filter_rate FROM rl_step WHERE entity_filter_rate IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' ORDER BY time

defaults.noValue: GRPO runs only: run healthy_grpo, reward_hacking, or reward_hacking_unwatched

panels.title: GRPO training reward
panels.description: 10-step moving average. What the training grader pays.

targets.rawSql: SELECT time, scenario, AVG(reward) OVER (PARTITION BY scenario, run_id ORDER BY time ROWS BETWEEN 9 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS reward FROM rl_step WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' ORDER BY time

defaults.noValue: GRPO runs only: run healthy_grpo, reward_hacking, or reward_hacking_unwatched

panels.title: Held-out SQL execution accuracy (independent of reward)

targets.rawSql: SELECT time, scenario, exec_accuracy FROM eval WHERE phase = 'grpo' AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' ORDER BY time

defaults.noValue: GRPO runs only: run healthy_grpo, reward_hacking, or reward_hacking_unwatched

panels.title: Label-free signals, no gold answers needed: KL to the reference and policy entropy
panels.description: Computed from the policy's own token probabilities at every GRPO step (10-step moving averages, nats), so they need no gold SQL, grader, or held-out set. Policy entropy (solid): mean per-token entropy of the next-token distribution; it falls as the policy narrows onto one kind of answer. Sample NLL (dashed): mean negative log-likelihood of the tokens actually sampled. KL to reference (dotted, right axis): how far the policy has moved from the base model, before SFT (the adapters disabled), so it starts above 0. These show that the policy is changing, not whether the change is right; held-out accuracy shows that.

targets.rawSql: SELECT time, concat(scenario, ' entropy') AS series, AVG(entropy) OVER (PARTITION BY run_id ORDER BY time ROWS BETWEEN 9 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS value FROM rl_step WHERE entropy IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' UNION ALL SELECT time, concat(scenario, ' sample NLL') AS series, AVG(sample_nll) OVER (PARTITION BY run_id ORDER BY time ROWS BETWEEN 9 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS value FROM rl_step WHERE sample_nll IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' UNION ALL SELECT time, concat(scenario, ' KL to reference') AS series, AVG(kl) OVER (PARTITION BY run_id ORDER BY time ROWS BETWEEN 9 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS value FROM rl_step WHERE kl IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' ORDER BY time

defaults.noValue: GRPO runs only: run healthy_grpo, reward_hacking, or reward_hacking_unwatched

panels.title: Response length (tokens)
panels.description: 10-step moving average.

targets.rawSql: SELECT time, scenario, AVG(resp_len) OVER (PARTITION BY scenario, run_id ORDER BY time ROWS BETWEEN 9 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS resp_len FROM rl_step WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' ORDER BY time

defaults.noValue: GRPO runs only: run healthy_grpo, reward_hacking, or reward_hacking_unwatched

panels.title: Sampled SQL (GRPO): what the model writes, and what it is paid for
panels.description: The highest-reward candidate every few GRPO steps (real Trainium runs). reward is what the training grader paid; correct is whether its result matches the gold query's result.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time, scenario, step, reward, exec_match AS correct, sql, question
FROM sample WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 50

defaults.noValue: GRPO runs only: run healthy_grpo, reward_hacking, or reward_hacking_unwatched

targets.rawSql:
SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '10 seconds', time) AS time, scenario, avg(util_pct) AS util
FROM neuron_hw WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' GROUP BY 1, scenario ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Data plane: InfluxDB 3 Enterprise under the watchdog (writes on the ingest node, reads on the query node)
Series cardinality by measurement (selected time range)
panels.description: Distinct tag combinations per measurement in the selected time range. Per-layer and per-head statistics are widest; everything else grows with runs and ranks. Whole database: ignores the Runs and Run selectors. Heavy: it scans every point in the range, on the query node that also serves the trainers' control polls, so a wide range over millions of series slows the polls (and, at 10 million series on db.influx.medium nodes, fails).

targets.rawSql: SELECT 'train_step' AS measurement, COUNT(DISTINCT concat_ws('|', local_rank, node, phase, rank, run_id, scenario)) AS series FROM train_step WHERE $__timeFilter(time) UNION ALL SELECT 'layer_stats' AS measurement, COUNT(DISTINCT concat_ws('|', layer, local_rank, module, node, phase, rank, run_id, scenario)) AS series FROM layer_stats WHERE $__timeFilter(time) UNION ALL SELECT 'attn_stats' AS measurement, COUNT(DISTINCT concat_ws('|', head, layer, local_rank, node, phase, rank, run_id, scenario)) AS series FROM attn_stats WHERE $__timeFilter(time) UNION ALL SELECT 'rl_candidate' AS measurement, COUNT(DISTINCT concat_ws('|', candidate, phase, question_id, question_shape, rank, result_class, run_id, scenario)) AS series FROM rl_candidate WHERE $__timeFilter(time) UNION ALL SELECT 'rl_prompt' AS measurement, COUNT(DISTINCT concat_ws('|', phase, prompt_id, prompt_shape, run_id, scenario)) AS series FROM rl_prompt WHERE $__timeFilter(time) UNION ALL SELECT 'eval_question' AS measurement, COUNT(DISTINCT concat_ws('|', eval_set, phase, question_id, question_type, run_id, scenario, window)) AS series FROM eval_question WHERE $__timeFilter(time) UNION ALL SELECT 'run_info' AS measurement, COUNT(DISTINCT concat_ws('|', grader, model, phase, run_id, scenario, seed, watched)) AS series FROM run_info WHERE $__timeFilter(time) UNION ALL SELECT 'neuron_runtime' AS measurement, COUNT(DISTINCT concat_ws('|', phase, run_id, runtime, scenario)) AS series FROM neuron_runtime WHERE $__timeFilter(time) UNION ALL SELECT 'host_cpu' AS measurement, COUNT(DISTINCT concat_ws('|', cpu, phase, run_id, scenario)) AS series FROM host_cpu WHERE $__timeFilter(time) UNION ALL SELECT 'host_mem' AS measurement, COUNT(DISTINCT concat_ws('|', phase, run_id, scenario)) AS series FROM host_mem WHERE $__timeFilter(time) UNION ALL SELECT 'neuron_hw' AS measurement, COUNT(DISTINCT concat_ws('|', neuron_core, phase, rank, run_id, scenario)) AS series FROM COUNT(DISTINCT concat_ws('|', phase, run_id, scenario)) AS series FROM rl_step WHERE $__timeFilter(time) UNION ALL SELECT 'sample' AS measurement, COUNT(DISTINCT concat_ws('|', phase, run_id, phase, run_id, scenario)) AS series FROM control_poll WHERE $__timeFilter(time) ORDER BY series DESC

panels.title: Calls per second (peak in the time range)
panels.description: Writes: successful write requests from the Flink InfluxDB connector's two sinks (telemetry, and incidents with step summaries) to the ingest node (each carries a batch of points), and points per second. Reads: control polls/s is what every trainer and simulated run reported polling (control_poll telemetry); SQL queries/s is every query the query node logged (system.queries: control polls plus this dashboard).

targets.rawSql: SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '1 minute', time) AS time, sum(polls) / 60.0 AS "Control polls/s" FROM control_poll WHERE $__timeFilter(time) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '1 minute', issue_time) AS time, count(*) / 60.0 AS "SQL queries/s" FROM system.queries WHERE $__timeFilter(issue_time) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Database size (selected time range)
panels.description: Counted from the measurements themselves, in the selected time range: points, distinct series (tag combinations), and measurements. Whole database: ignores the Runs and Run selectors. Heavy, like Series cardinality: keep the range short.

'control_poll' AS measurement, COUNT(*) AS points, COUNT(DISTINCT concat_ws('|', endpoint, phase, run_id, scenario)) AS series FROM control_poll WHERE $__timeFilter(time))

panels.title: Latency of every call: dots are SQL queries the query node served; lines are write percentiles
panels.description: Dots: end-to-end latency of every SQL query the query node logged (system.queries, up to 10,000 kept), split into control polls (the trainers' incident queries) and dashboard queries. Lines: write latency p50 and p99 of the Flink connector's write calls to the ingest node, per minute (CloudWatch), for the telemetry sink and (dotted) the control sink, which writes the incidents; and the pollers' own p50 round trip (control_poll telemetry, client side, includes the network). Log scale.

targets.rawSql: SELECT issue_time AS time, arrow_cast(end2end_duration, 'Int64') / 1e6 AS "control poll" FROM system.queries WHERE success AND end2end_duration IS NOT NULL AND (strpos(query_text, 'AS time_ns FROM incident') > 0 AND strpos(query_text, 'system.queries') = 0) AND $__timeFilter(issue_time) ORDER BY issue_time

SELECT issue_time AS time, arrow_cast(end2end_duration, 'Int64') / 1e6 AS "dashboard query" FROM system.queries WHERE success AND end2end_duration IS NOT NULL AND NOT (strpos(query_text, 'AS time_ns FROM incident') > 0 AND strpos(query_text, 'system.queries') = 0) AND $__timeFilter(issue_time) ORDER BY issue_time
SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '1 minute', time) AS time, median(latency_p50_ms) AS "control poll p50 (client)" FROM control_poll WHERE $__timeFilter(time) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
